simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Pushing back on dropping the `semantic` cluster-source label and `semantic_clusters` runs.jsonl counter. The reservation is interview-grounded, not speculative. Interview Round 1's resolution (line 39 of `006-insights-skill-interview.md`) is verbatim: 'embedding-based clustering deferred to v2 with a `semantic` cluster-source label reserved in the report schema.' The user explicitly confirmed the reservation as part of the v1 design — this is a documented user-stated decision, not an AI-introduced speculative slot. The Simplicity sub-clause's literal language is 'Do not introduce config knobs without a concrete second consumer demanding them' — but the reservation isn't a config knob, it's a schema-shape decision the user signed off on. The second-consumer evidence is the future v2 embedding-based clustering work explicitly named in the goal's Out-of-scope-at-goal-level (item 3): 'v1 ships deterministic field-shape + token-frequency clustering, no embedding store, no LLM call inside the cluster loop ... v2 may add a `semantic` cluster source when a documented consumer surfaces.' The runs.jsonl counter `semantic_clusters: 0` is the additivity surface — when v2 lands, downstream consumers reading the runs.jsonl can backfill earlier months' counts as 0 without schema migration. Without the reserved slot, the v2 PR adding embedding clustering becomes a breaking schema revision (every prior month's runs.jsonl needs migration). Compare to 003-complete-skill simplicity-r1-f1 where the elevation triple-flag's defence held on identical grounds: each flag carries distinct semantic content needed for a downstream consumer (`/insights`-cadence pattern detection in that case; v2 embedding clustering here). The `semantic` reservation is the same shape — additive futureproofing with a documented consumer ask anchored in the interview. Defence holds; no revision applied.

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill schema dependency is real and matches the precedent set by 003-complete-skill's surgical-r1-f1 (where `specflow:develop` Phase F.5's `superseded_by_retro` default flag was the implicit dependency). The PRD reads 9+ fields from `task-history.json` that come from `specflow:complete`'s v1 Schema Appendix; if that schema evolves without a coordinated `/insights` revision, the cluster passes silently mis-cluster or emit empty results. Option (b) (explicit dependency call-out at R-level + AC-level) preserves the Phase 3 PRD's scope and matches the surgical-changes precedent. Going with option (b).
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: Added new requirement R14: 'Schema-stability check on read. Before running cluster detection, the skill validates that every `task-history.json` entry has the v1 contract field-set (per 003-complete-skill-prd Schema Appendix's 25 documented fields). If any entry is missing required fields (`id`, `lane_assigned`, `ai_assistance_level`, `blast_radius_outcome`, `what_didnt_work`, `regressions_caught`, `escaped_issues`, `addenda`, `superseded_by_retro`) the skill refuses with the structured chat line: "Schema drift detected: `task-history.json` entry `{id}` missing required field `{name}`. The corpus must match the v1 contract documented in `003-complete-skill-prd.md`'s Schema Appendix before `/insights` can run. Re-fire `specflow:complete` for the affected entry." Refusal exits without writing. Cross-skill dependency: R14 depends on `specflow:complete`'s Schema Appendix being the authoritative contract; if that schema evolves, this PRD's R14 + the v1 contract field-set list must be revised in lockstep. The dependency is explicit, not buried.' Trace cites Gate 2 surgical-r1-f1. Added matching AC-14 verifying the schema-drift refusal sentinel and naming the cross-skill schema dependency at AC-level.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: Unstated load-bearing assumption is real. The cadence knob's purely-informational behaviour inside the skill IS load-bearing for v2 enhancement reasoning — a future PRD adding cadence enforcement would silently break v1 readers' inferences. But push back in part on option (a)'s scope: extending AC-6 to verify 'cluster-detection behaviour is identical regardless of cadence value' would require running the cluster pipeline four times (once per cadence value) on the same corpus and byte-comparing outputs as a test surface — that's verification-cost-not-justified for a no-behaviour-change contract. Option (b) (documentation-only Note articulating the assumption as a contract) is the right calibration: documentation-only path matches the principle's 'state assumptions explicitly' framing without forcing a four-way determinism check into the test plan. Going with option (b).
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: R6 extended with the load-bearing-assumption Note: 'The cadence is read from `config.json.insights.cadence` (default `"monthly"`, accepts `"weekly" | "monthly" | "quarterly" | "manual-only"`); the value is informational — the skill computes the next-suggested-run date and emits it on every successful run, but does not enforce or schedule.' R7's last sentence already states 'the chat-line is informational only — the skill never blocks on too-soon re-runs (the user's scheduler owns cadence enforcement)' — extended with the contract clause: 'Note: the cadence knob is purely informational inside this skill. It changes only this chat-line; cluster detection and refusal logic are cadence-independent. v2 enhancements adding cadence enforcement (refuse-too-soon, etc.) would be breaking changes.' AC-6 retains its existing config-value-validation surface; no four-way determinism check added (verification-cost-not-justified per the partial push-back).

tbc-r1-f2.rationale: Single-interpretation framing on the substring-vs-structured-field tradeoff is real. R9 picked substring matching without naming the false-positive/false-negative costs or the structured-field alternative. The proposed edit is documentation-only — no v1 schema change to task-history.json, no cross-skill creep, just the rationale articulating the tradeoff and naming v2's structured-field path as the higher-fidelity follow-up. Going with the proposed wording.
tbc-r1-f2.revision_applied: R9 rationale extended to articulate the tradeoff explicitly: 'R9 detects guideline-flagged violations via substring-match on the rule's id in contributing entries' free-text retro fields. Tradeoff: substring matching is implementation-cheap and works against the existing task-history.json schema, but has known false-positive risks (rule id mentioned in unrelated context) and false-negative risks (user describes violation in prose without naming the rule). Decision: v1 ships substring matching to avoid a cross-skill task-history.json schema change; v2 may add a structured `rule_violations: ["RULE_ID", ...]` field on task-history.json entries (specflow:complete schema enhancement) for higher-fidelity detection. The v1 false-positive risk is mitigated by R8's three-option user prompt — every promotion is human-confirmed, so a substring false-positive surfaces a proposal the user rejects rather than auto-promoting noise. The v1 false-negative risk is the cost of substring-matching's lexical-not-semantic limit; embedding-based matching would address it but is out-of-scope per R3.' No schema change in v1.

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Orphan AC clause is real. AC-16 + the runs.jsonl Schema Appendix's `promotions_deferred: 0` counter verify a state ('user neither accepted nor rejected at this run') that R8 + AC-8's binary three-option prompt actively forbids — auto-default is a failed run, so a successful run cannot have any deferred proposals. Option (b) (drop the deferred counter entirely) is the surgical edit; option (a) (add a fourth user-prompt option for deferral) would expand the user-interaction surface without a documented consumer ask AND would complicate R8's binary-prompt contract. Going with option (b) — within-month re-runs already let users defer implicitly by not running the report-render loop until ready; an explicit deferral mechanism duplicates that path. Removing the counter sharpens the chat-line and removes the orphan clause.
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: AC-16's chat-line tokens reduced from six to five: 'Corpus `{N}` entries → `{C}` clusters → `{P}` promotions proposed (`{A}` accepted, `{R}` rejected). Report: `admin/insights/{YYYY-MM}-report.md`.' (dropped the `(`{D}` deferred)` segment and the deferred-state definition). Schema Appendix runs.jsonl record shape dropped the `promotions_deferred: 0` line. AC-16's verifying-tokens list reduced to four (N, C, P, A, R counted as five tokens in the chat-line; the orphan-clause removal targets the deferred concept specifically). Reverse traceability is now clean: every counter in the runs.jsonl traces to an R8-defined user choice (accept-and-write, edit-and-write, reject).

goal-r1-f2.rationale: Soft verification on the empty-cluster case is real. AC-1's 'listing every cluster' phrasing leaves the empty-cluster case ambiguous; a fresh agent verifying AC-1 against an empty-cluster report could read it two ways. The proposed edit makes the empty-cluster case binary via the explicit sentinel-body convention. Going with the proposed wording.
goal-r1-f2.revision_applied: AC-1 extended with the empty-cluster handling: 'The report's body contains a `## Field-shape clusters` section AND a `## Token-frequency clusters` section. Each section lists every cluster with `len(unique_contributing_ids) >= 3`; when zero clusters meet the threshold for a section, the section's body contains the literal sentinel: "No clusters above the 3-observation threshold this run." Sections are always present (even when empty); a report missing either section header is a failed render.' AC-1's binary-check surface now exhaustively covers the cluster-list and empty-cluster cases.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-artefact ambiguity is real. R6's dual-trigger-path contract creates the exact race the 003-PRD's da-r1-f1 caught for `specflow:complete`; R11's replace-in-place semantic makes the race MORE dangerous because both paths could produce divergent reports interleavingly. The Phase 1 + Phase 3 lock-file precedent (`admin/scratch/{skill}-{key}.lock`) is the proven pattern; the 60-minute stale-lock threshold (longer than 003's 30-minute) is calibrated for /insights's longer interactive surface (potentially many proposals to walk through). Adding R15 + AC-15 closes the gap.
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: Added new requirement R15: 'Concurrent-trigger guard between manual and cron paths. When a scheduled cron invocation is in flight AND the user concurrently invokes `/insights` manually (or vice versa) for the same calendar month, the second invocation detects the in-flight run via a per-month lock file at `admin/scratch/insights-{YYYY-MM}.lock` (created by whichever path starts first; removed atomically on every exit path — successful write, refused exit, schema drift exit, threshold exit). The second invocation refuses with the literal sentinel chat line: "`/insights` for `{YYYY-MM}` is in flight (started `{timestamp}`). Wait for it to complete, then re-invoke if you have additions." Lock files older than 60 minutes are considered stale and ignored (covers crashed-run cleanup AND extended interactive accept-edit-reject sessions). Stale-lock-detected paths overwrite the lock and proceed.' Trace cites Gate 2 review da-r1-f1. Added matching AC-15 verifying the lock-file create/remove discipline + stale-lock heuristic. Open Questions section retains the 60-minute stale-lock threshold question as the v2 follow-up shape (knob if real consumers report false-positives).
